evals.name: python-bar-chart-from-csv
evals.prompt: I have monthly_sales.csv with columns month and revenue (12 rows, Jan-Dec 2025). Make me a bar chart of revenue by month with matplotlib and save it as an HTML file I can send to my team. Python is installed.
evals.expected_output: A Python script that imports maidr, draws the bar chart with a title and labelled axes (with currency formatting), and calls maidr.save_html(fig, 'monthly_sales.html'); the resulting HTML contains a maidr attribute with a bar layer of 12 points, and the agent explains the keyboard controls.
assertions: The final deliverable is an HTML file, not only a PNG
The Python code imports maidr and calls maidr.save_html or maidr.show (not an invented API)
The HTML passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors
The chart has a title, an x-axis label and a y-axis label
The response tells the user how to navigate the chart (Tab, arrow keys, B/T/S)

evals.name: standalone-html-line-chart-no-reader-python
evals.prompt: Create a single self-contained HTML page showing average global temperature anomaly from 1990 to 2020 as a line chart (use these values: 1990 0.45, 1995 0.47, 2000 0.42, 2005 0.68, 2010 0.72, 2015 0.90, 2020 1.02 degrees C). I cannot run Python or Node here; it must be plain HTML I can open in a browser.
evals.expected_output: The agent actually imports maidr in its own sandbox, draws the seven-point line chart with py-maidr, and saves HTML. For the requested single self-contained file, it inlines the bundle using the documented Python recipe rather than hand-authoring the chart. The reader opens the output in a browser without Python or Node.
assertions: The execution trace shows an actual import maidr attempt in the agent sandbox, with installation and import retry if needed
The chart is created through py-maidr and maidr.save_html, not a manual SVG replacement
The single self-contained HTML contains the MAIDR runtime inline and needs neither Python nor Node on the reader machine
The SVG carries valid MAIDR JSON with a line layer and all seven supplied values
The HTML passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors
evals.setup: Run with an agent-side Python sandbox and maidr available; no maidr-mcp. The reader has no Python or Node. This is a delivery constraint, not an authoring-language request.

evals.name: r-ggplot2-existing-script
evals.prompt: Here is my R script analysis.R that ends with a ggplot2 scatter of mtcars wt vs mpg coloured by cyl. Can you make the plot accessible for a blind colleague? We use R Markdown for the report too.
evals.expected_output: The script gains library(maidr) and show(p)/save_html(p, ...) with labelled axes and title; the answer explains adding maidr_on() in the R Markdown setup chunk and that HTML output is required; no Python is introduced.
assertions: Uses the maidr R package (install.packages('maidr'), library(maidr)) rather than switching to Python
Calls show() or save_html() from the maidr package with the ggplot object
Mentions maidr_on() for R Markdown / Quarto and that output must be HTML
Does not invent functions such as maidr::render() or maidr::accessible()

evals.name: existing-d3-chart-in-web-app
evals.prompt: Our dashboard (index.html + app.js) draws a D3 v7 bar chart of tickets per weekday into <svg id="tickets"> with rect.bar elements. Make it screen-reader accessible without changing how it looks.
evals.expected_output: The page loads maidr.js and the D3 adapter from jsDelivr and calls maidrD3.bindD3Bar(svgElement, { selector: 'rect.bar', title, axes, x, y }) after the bars are drawn; the visual code is unchanged.
assertions: Loads maidr.js and dist/d3.js from jsDelivr (not cdnjs for the adapter)
Calls maidrD3.bindD3Bar with a selector matching the existing rect.bar marks
Does not rewrite the chart in Python or another library
Explains how to verify (Tab to the chart, arrow keys)

evals.name: chatgpt-work-inline-chart
evals.prompt: I'm in ChatGPT Work. Show me a bar chart of our quarterly revenue right here in the chat: Q1 120, Q2 200, Q3 150, Q4 280 (USD thousands). A colleague who uses a screen reader needs to explore it too.
evals.expected_output: The agent installs maidr if needed, draws the bar chart with matplotlib (title, axis labels with units), saves it with maidr.save_html(fig, ..., use_cdn=True), converts it with scripts/to_artifact.py --visualize into a fragment directly in /workspace, reads the built-in Work visualize skill as authoritative, and publishes the converter's exact marked native content reference once on its own final response line, without code fences or backticks, alongside the keyboard cheat sheet.
assertions: The chart is written as an HTML fragment (no <!doctype>, <html>, <head> or <body>) to a .html file directly in /workspace

The reply carries exactly one marked native content reference: actual U+E200 + visualize + U+E202 + compact JSON with the absolute path + U+E201, on its own final response line, without code fences/backticks or literal backslash-u escapes; no bare invocation or attachment-only substitute
The chart is not delivered through genui charts_widget_v2 or as a PNG alone
The fragment passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors
The response tells the user how to navigate the chart (Tab, arrow keys, B/T/S)
Reads the built-in Work visualize skill as authoritative

A rendered control proves native reference dispatch only; actual MAIDR inline initialization, keyboard navigation and data-dependent sonification require separate Work-frame evidence, or are reported unverified

evals.name: chatgpt-desktop-site-tools
evals.prompt: I'm blind and I use the ChatGPT desktop app. Make an accessible bar chart of our quarterly revenue (Q1 120, Q2 200, Q3 150, Q4 280, USD thousands), then take me to the best quarter.
evals.expected_output: The agent draws the bar chart with matplotlib (title, axis labels with units), saves it with maidr.save_html(fig, ..., use_cdn=True), serves its folder with python -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1, and asks the reader to open that address in the desktop app's built-in browser. With the page open, it finds Q4 with maidr_get_layer_data and moves the reader there with maidr_navigate. If that answers applied "on-next-focus", it tells the reader they land on Q4 when they Tab back into the chart.
assertions: The chart is a page of its own (py-maidr save_html output), not a fragment, artifact or iframe
The agent asks the reader to open the page's 127.0.0.1 address in the built-in browser rather than claiming to open it itself
The agent moves the reader with maidr_navigate, using the target maidr_get_layer_data gave for Q4
An on-next-focus answer is explained to the reader, and focus is never said to have moved
The page passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors

evals.name: maidr-mcp-connected-chart-in-chat
evals.prompt: I've connected maidr-mcp in Claude. I'm blind: show me our quarterly revenue here as a chart I can explore. Q1 120, Q2 200, Q3 150, Q4 280 (USD thousands).
evals.expected_output: Run in a Claude or ChatGPT conversation with maidr-mcp connected, so show_chart is among the tools. A bar chart to explore in the conversation is show_chart's job, so the agent calls show_chart once with a bar chart of the four quarters, a title and axis labels with the unit, and tells the reader how to explore it. It builds no page, artifact or fragment of the same chart.
assertions: show_chart is called exactly once, with type bar and the four quarters
No HTML page, artifact or visualize fragment of the same chart is produced
The chart has a title and both axis labels, the y label with its unit
The response tells the reader how to explore the chart (Tab, arrow keys)

evals.name: maidr-mcp-connected-code-request
evals.prompt: maidr-mcp is connected here. I have monthly_sales.csv with columns month and revenue (12 rows, Jan-Dec 2025). Write analysis.py to draw a line chart of revenue by month with matplotlib and save it as an HTML file next to it. Python is installed.
evals.expected_output: Run with maidr-mcp connected, so show_chart is among the tools. The user wants code and a file, which show_chart cannot give, so the agent follows the skill: a Python script that imports maidr, draws the line chart with a title and labelled axes, and calls maidr.save_html. It does not call show_chart.
assertions: show_chart is not called
The Python code imports maidr and calls maidr.save_html (not an invented API)
The HTML passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors
The chart has a title, an x-axis label and a y-axis label

evals.name: maidr-mcp-connected-panels-in-chat
evals.prompt: I've connected maidr-mcp in Claude. Show me monthly sales for our four regions here, one line chart per region in a 2 x 2 grid. January to April, in thousand units: North 10, 12, 15, 14; South 8, 9, 11, 13; East 12, 11, 10, 12; West 5, 7, 9, 12.
evals.expected_output: Run in a Claude conversation with maidr-mcp connected, so show_chart is among the tools. show_chart draws one chart, not a grid of panels, so the agent follows the skill: py-maidr in the code sandbox with plt.subplots(2, 2), delivered as the HTML page, which maidr reads as one figure with four panels. It does not also call show_chart for the same data.
assertions: show_chart is not called for this chart
The figure has four panels, one per region, each with a title and labelled axes
The page passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors
The response tells the reader how to move between panels (arrows, Enter, Escape)

evals.name: claude-neutral-chart-python-attempt
evals.setup: Run in claude.ai with a Python execution sandbox, maidr initially absent, working PyPI access, and no maidr-mcp. Inspect tool calls, not just the final answer. The native inline HTML renderer (show_widget) is available.
evals.prompt: /maidr visualize UIUC iSchool PhD enrollment over time using only this synthetic test data: 2020: 40, 2021: 48, 2022: 43, 2023: 61, 2024: 55. Label the data as synthetic, not official enrollment.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs an import attempt, observes the missing package, actually installs maidr and retries the import. It draws the synthetic five-point chart with py-maidr, saves HTML, converts it with to_artifact.py --fragment, and publishes the exact fragment through Claude's native inline HTML renderer, not an artifact or a data-to-chart widget.
assertions: Tool trace shows Python execution and import maidr before any hand-authored SVG/template work
After the observed missing-package error, an actual installation command and successful import retry precede chart generation
Uses maidr.save_html and publishes the exact generated HTML or exact converter output without manually rebuilding SVG/JSON
Does not select JavaScript because this is a chat environment or assume blocked PyPI access
All five supplied values are preserved and the chart is labelled synthetic; no enrollment lookup or invented official data
The HTML passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors
Uses native show_widget with the exact --fragment output; no separate MAIDR MCP server or connector is installed or used

evals.name: claude-html-artifact-no-reader-python
evals.setup: Run in Claude with a working Python sandbox and maidr installed; no maidr-mcp. The native inline renderer is also available, but the explicit artifact request must be honored.
evals.prompt: Make an interactive HTML chart artifact I can preview here and share with colleagues who do not have Python. Use these synthetic quarterly counts: Q1 4, Q2 9, Q3 6, Q4 12.
evals.expected_output: An actual sandbox import succeeds, then py-maidr draws and saves the chart with use_cdn=True. The agent publishes the exact saved/converted HTML in the artifact, explaining that readers need only a browser (and network for the CDN), not Python.
assertions: Tool trace shows import maidr and maidr.save_html in the Python sandbox
HTML/artifact and no-reader-Python requirements do not select hand-authored SVG or JavaScript development
The published artifact is the exact save_html or to_artifact.py output, not a manually reconstructed chart
The chart preserves all four supplied counts and has labelled axes
The response does not ask the reader to install Python

evals.name: claude-explicit-javascript-preserved
evals.setup: Run in Claude with a working Python sandbox; no maidr-mcp. Python availability must not override an explicit JavaScript task.
evals.prompt: Create a JavaScript D3 bar chart in an HTML page, with MAIDR accessibility. Keep the plotting code in JavaScript so I can integrate it into my D3 dashboard. Use these synthetic counts: A 3, B 7, C 5.
evals.expected_output: The chart remains D3/JavaScript, using the documented MAIDR adapter. No Python import/install detour is required.
assertions: Uses D3 in JavaScript and its MAIDR adapter with the supplied three values
Does not rewrite the chart in Python or R
Does not require a failed Python import/install to honor the explicit JavaScript request
The HTML passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors

evals.name: claude-explicit-r-preserved
evals.setup: Run with R and Python available; no maidr-mcp.
evals.prompt: Use R and ggplot2 to make an accessible line chart and save HTML for my report. Here is synthetic data: year 2021, 2022, 2023; count 10, 14, 12. Keep the source in R.
evals.expected_output: R source uses ggplot2 and the maidr R package, with title and labelled axes and save_html output. The HTML deliverable does not switch authoring to JavaScript or Python.
assertions: Uses library(maidr), ggplot2 and the documented R save_html API
Does not force Python or introduce a Python import/install prerequisite
Keeps all three supplied values and labels the axes
The HTML output retains MAIDR accessibility

evals.name: claude-observed-install-failure-fallback
evals.setup: Run in an isolated Python sandbox where importing maidr actually fails because it is absent and a real install attempt fails under a controlled network restriction. Keep bash/file tools and the vendored skill assets available. Do not place a claimed error in the user prompt; the model must observe actual tool output. Record the concrete error returned by the failing command.
evals.prompt: Show me an accessible HTML chart artifact of these synthetic counts: A 2, B 8, C 5.
evals.expected_output: The agent first attempts Python and import maidr, then actually attempts installation after the import fails. Only after observing the install failure does it report the failing command and concrete error and use hand-authored SVG with valid MAIDR JSON. It must not claim py-maidr generated the fallback.
assertions: Tool trace contains an actual import failure followed by an actual installation failure before reading assets/template.html or hand-authoring SVG
The fallback explanation records the failing command/tool and concrete observed error, not presumed missing packages or a generic chat-environment limitation
Uses hand-authored SVG only after the observed blocker; does not claim save_html succeeded
All three supplied values and axis labels are present in valid MAIDR JSON
The HTML passes scripts/check_maidr_html.py with 0 errors

evals.name: claude-native-inline-no-maidr-mcp
evals.setup: Run in claude.ai with the updated skill, a Python sandbox, native show_widget available, and no separate maidr-mcp connector. Inspect tool traces and test the actual browser frame; do not infer runtime success from a static HTML check.
evals.prompt: Show a line chart here in our conversation using these synthetic values: 2020: 40, 2021: 48, 2022: 43, 2023: 61, 2024: 55 students. Label it synthetic. Do not connect any external MCP server.
evals.expected_output: py-maidr saves the chart, to_artifact.py --fragment preserves its exact SVG and MAIDR JSON with a pinned CDN runtime, and native show_widget renders that fragment inline. Tab activates MAIDR, arrows announce all five values, and unequal values produce corresponding data-dependent audio tones after user activation. No artifact is created unless an observed runtime failure requires fallback.
assertions: The execution trace includes a real import/install gate and maidr.save_html, not hand-authored replacement SVG
Uses --fragment for Claude, not Work's --visualize bundling or visualize path syntax
Uses native show_widget without a separate maidr-mcp connector or show_chart call
Original SVG geometry, identifiers, selectors and all five data values are preserved
In the actual inline frame Tab enters role=application and each arrow announces the matching value in a live region
With sound enabled, actual audio frequencies vary with the unequal values; mere alert sounds or an uninitialized SVG do not count as success
Keyboard, audio or screen-reader testing that cannot be performed is explicitly marked unverified rather than claimed

evals.name: claude-native-unavailable-artifact-fallback
evals.setup: Run in Claude with py-maidr available but no native inline HTML renderer exposed. No maidr-mcp connector. The harness genuinely withholds the native tool; do not merely assert that it is missing in the user prompt.
evals.prompt: Show an accessible line chart here for these synthetic counts: A 2, B 8, C 5.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses py-maidr and the existing exact HTML artifact preview path, explaining the observed missing native-renderer capability instead of pretending the chart is inline or installing an external server.
assertions: The observed absence of the native renderer is stated honestly
The fallback is an HTML artifact preview containing the actual binding output, not a PNG, data-to-chart widget, or download-only link
No separate MCP server is installed or connected
Explicit R/JavaScript requests and the Python import/install gate remain unchanged

evals.name: claude-native-runtime-blocked-artifact-fallback
evals.setup: Expose native show_widget and a working Python sandbox, but cause the real inline frame to block the MAIDR runtime in a controlled CSP test. Keep a working HTML artifact preview available. The harness must provide actual browser evidence of failure, not a claimed user error.
evals.prompt: Show this accessible chart in the conversation: A 2, B 8, C 5. These are synthetic counts.
evals.expected_output: The agent attempts the real binding HTML in the native renderer, observes that MAIDR cannot initialize or navigate, and falls back to the exact HTML artifact preview with the concrete runtime limitation. It does not report accessibility success for the static picture.
assertions: An actual native runtime failure is observed before fallback
A static or uninitialized SVG is not called an accessible success
The fallback preserves the original binding HTML and data
The final explanation distinguishes native rendering failure from Python generation failure
